en: The Eighth Adhyāya of the First Aṣṭaka.
The sūktas 113–121 of the First Maṇḍala.
113. The one hundred thirteenth sūkta, beginning ⟦ಇದಂ ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠಂ⟧
The application (viniyoga) of the sūkta, and the seer, deity and metres.
The origin of the time of dawn (Uṣas), etc.
Discussion of the sameness and difference of Night and Dawn.
The differences and non-differences of Night and Dawn.
Explanation of the meaning of the word ⟦ವಿಸದೃಶಾ⟧, etc.
Explanation of the meaning of the words ⟦ಪರಾಯತೀನಾಂ⟧, ⟦ಆಯತೀನಾಂ⟧ and other words.
The pervasion of the time of dawn through the past, future and present.
Explanation of the words ⟦ಸುಮ್ನಾವರೀ⟧, ⟦ಸೂನೃತಾ⟧ and others.
The mutual relation of the present and past times of Dawn.
Explanation of the meaning of the word ⟦ಅಸು⟧, etc.
The use of the word ⟦ಅಸ್ಮೇ⟧ in all seven cases, with examples.
The meaning of the words ⟦ಅದಿತೇರನೀಕಂ⟧.
114. The one hundred fourteenth sūkta, beginning ⟦ಇಮಾ ರುದ್ರಾಯ⟧
The application (viniyoga) of the sūkta.
The seer, deity and metres.
Explanation of the word ⟦ರುದ್ರ⟧, etc.
Explanation of the meaning of the word ⟦ಕ್ಷಯದ್ವೀರ⟧.
The subject of Manu.
Discussion of the meaning of the word ⟦ವರಾಹ⟧.
The Aṅgirases are also called Varāhas.
Rudra as the father of the Marut deities.
Explanation of the meaning of the word ⟦ಆಯುಃ⟧.
Discussion of the meaning of the word ⟦ದ್ವಿಬರ್ಹ⟧.
115. The one hundred fifteenth sūkta, beginning ⟦ಚಿತ್ರಂ ದೇವಾನಾಂ⟧
The application (viniyoga) of the sūkta.
The seer, deity and metres.
The Sun as the Self of the whole moving and unmoving world.
Explanation of the meaning of the word ⟦ಯುಗ⟧.
The greatness of the Sun's horses.
The greatness of the rising and setting of the Sun.
116. The one hundred sixteenth sūkta, beginning ⟦ನಾಸತ್ಯಾಭ್ಯಾಂ⟧
The application (viniyoga) of the sūkta.
The seer, deity and metres.
The birth-story of the seer called ⟦ಕಕ್ಷೀನಾನ್⟧, etc.
The subject of the royal seer Vimada.
Explanation of the meaning of the word for the sacred grass spread at the sacrifice, etc.
How the she-ass, the vehicle of the Aśvin deities, won in the contest of the gods.
The various vehicles of Indra and the other deities.
The svayaṃvara of Sūryā, the daughter of the Sun.
The subject of the king Tugra.
How the Aśvin deities saved Bhujyu, the son of Tugra, in the midst of the sea.
Explanation of the word ⟦ಸಮುದ್ರ⟧, etc.
How the Aśvin deities gave a white horse to the king Pedu.
The Aṅgirases are called Pajras.
The derivation of the word ⟦ಕಕ್ಷೀವಾನ್⟧.
How the Aśvin deities made honey flow with the hoof of their horse.
Explanation of the meaning of the word ⟦ಪುರಂಧಿ⟧.
How the Aśvin deities saved the seer Atri, whom the Asuras had thrown into a fire of husks to burn, by quenching that fire with cold water.
Explanation of the meaning of the word ⟦ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ⟧.
How the seer Gotama, thirsty, prayed to the Aśvin deities for water, and they brought a well of water from a distant place to his side and quenched his thirst.
How the Aśvin deities, seeing the seer Cyavana suffering from old age, gave him youth.
How they lifted up and saved the seer Vandana, who had fallen into a well in a deserted forest.
The story of the seer Dadhīca, and how Dadhīca taught the Madhu-vidyā to the Aśvin deities.
The legend told on this subject by Skandasvāmin.
How the horse's head came to the seer Dadhīca.
The opinion of the scholar Wilson on this subject.
How they granted a son called Hiraṇyahasta to the woman Vadhrimatī.
How the Aśvin deities freed a bird like the quail (a sparrow) from the mouth of the wolf and saved it.
Explanation of the meaning of the word ⟦ವೃಕ⟧.
How the Aśvin deities repaired the cut-off leg of the woman Viśpalā, a relative of the king Khela, the priest of Agastya.

How the Aśvin deities restored sight, as before, to Ṛjrāśva, whom his father had made blind in anger because Ṛjrāśva had cut up a hundred sheep and given them as food to the she-ass, the vehicle of the Aśvin deities, when it was in the form of a wolf.
How the chariot of the Aśvin deities won in the contest of the gods.
The story of Divodāsa.
How the Aśvin deities showed favour to Jāhnavī, the daughter of the great seer Jahnu.
The subject of the king Jāhuṣa.
How the Aśvin deities saved the king Pṛthuśravas and a man called Vaśa.

How the seer Śara, tormented by thirst, was unable to drink the water of a deep well found on the way and praised the Aśvin deities, and they came and made the water of the well rise to the top and quenched Śara's thirst.
How they made the barren cow of the seer Śayu bear a calf and give milk.
How the Aśvin deities searched for Viṣṇāpva, the son of the king Viśvaka, who had run away, found him and gave him to his father.
How the Aśvin deities lifted up and saved the seer Rebha, who had been thrown into a well by the Asuras and had suffered for ten days.
117. The one hundred seventeenth sūkta, beginning ⟦ಮಧ್ವಃ ಸೋಮಸ್ಯ⟧
The application (viniyoga) of the sūkta.
The seer, deity and metres.
The first place of the Aśvin deities among the deities of the heavenly region.
Explanation of the meaning of the word ⟦ವಸಾತಿ⟧, etc.
Explanation of the meaning of the word ⟦ಪಂಚಜನ⟧.
How the Aśvin deities lifted up and saved the seer Rebha from the water.
How they lifted up and saved the seer Vandana from the well.
How they brought Viṣṇāpva and gave him to his father Viśvaka, and how they provided a husband for the woman Ghoṣā.
How they cured the seer Śyāva, who was suffering from leprosy, and how they gave eyes to the seer Kaṇva, the son of Nṛṣad, who could not see.
How they gave an excellent white horse to the king Pedu.
How they set right the cut-off leg of the woman Viśpalā, a relative of the king Khela, the priest of Agastya; and the birth-story of the seers Agastya and Vasiṣṭha.
How they lifted up Rebha from the well and saved him.
How they made the aged seer Cyavana young again; and that the daughter of the Sun mounted the chariot of the Aśvin deities.
How they saved Bhujyu, the son of Tugra, from the sea and brought him back.
How the Aśvin deities freed the bird called Vartikā from the mouth of the wolf.
How they slew the Asura called Viśvāñca.
How they gave sight to the blind seer Ṛjrāśva.
Explanation of the meaning of the word ⟦ಸೀಂ⟧, etc.
How they made the barren cow of the seer Śayu give milk.
How they rescued the wife of Vimada, carried off by the Asuras, and brought her back.
How the seer Dadhīca taught the Madhu-vidyā to the Aśvin deities.
How they granted a son called Hiraṇyahasta to the woman Vadhrimatī.
118. The one hundred eighteenth sūkta, beginning ⟦ಆ ವಾಂ ರಥಃ⟧
The application (viniyoga) of the sūkta, and the seer, deity and metres.
Description of the chariot of the Aśvin deities, etc.
How the Aśvin deities saved Nandana, Rebha, Bhujyu, Cyavana and others.
How they gave sight to the blind seer Kaṇva.

The many heroic deeds of the Aśvin deities: making the cow of the seer Śayu give milk, freeing the bird Vartikā from the mouth of the wolf, and joining another leg to the cut-off leg of the woman Viśpalā.
How they gave a white horse to the king Pedu.
119. The one hundred nineteenth sūkta, beginning ⟦ಆ ವಾಂ ರಥಂ ಪುರುಮಾಯಂ⟧
The application (viniyoga) of the sūkta, and the seer, deity and metres.
The greatness of the chariot of the Aśvin deities, etc.
How they saved Bhujyu and Divodāsa.
How the daughter of the Sun mounted the chariot of the Aśvin deities of her own accord.
How they lifted up and saved the seer Rebha from the well.
How they drove away the worn-out body of the seer Nandana and made him full of youth; and how they caused the seer Vāmadeva to be born from his mother's womb.
How they saved Bhujyu, who was sinking in the middle of the sea.
How the Aśvin deities made honey available to the bees.
That the seer Kakṣīvān is the chief among the thirty-three eminent descendants of Aṅgiras.
How they gave a divine horse to the king Pedu.
120. The one hundred twentieth sūkta, beginning ⟦ಕಾ ರಾಧದ್ದೋತ್ರಾ⟧
The application (viniyoga) of the sūkta, explanation of the metre, etc.
The seer, deity and metres.
How Ṛjrāśva, when blind, praised the Aśvin deities for the gift of sight.
The various meanings of the word ⟦ವೃಕ⟧.
Explanation of the meaning of the word ⟦ಸ್ತನಾಭುಜಃ⟧, etc.
Explanation of the meaning of the word ⟦ವಾಜಿನೀವತಿ⟧, etc.

The application (viniyoga) of the sūkta, and the seer, deity and metres.

Explanation of the meaning of the word ⟦ಪಯಃ⟧, etc.

Explanation of the meaning of the word ⟦ಏತಶ⟧.
